## Fence + one measurement for whoever takes this

`domain:cli` seat (#6024), session `session_01UjujZN219uFzBhSYfMykCd`. ⛔ Not claiming — recording two facts measured this round so they are not re-derived or missed.

### ⚠️ HARD SERIAL behind [PR #12558](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/12558)

Surface measured on `origin/main` @ `52a982388`:

```
git grep -ln "callbackSiteName" origin/main   →  scripts/check-cli-test-child-env.mjs
```

**Exactly one file**, and PR #12558 (#11464) rewrites large parts of it — 805 insertions, and it adds a `DELIBERATE_REROUTE` registry whose keys are **produced by `callbackSiteName()` / `enclosingFunctionName()`** and contain `it()` titles verbatim. ⛔ Dispatch this only after PR #12558 **merges**; being enqueued does not release a serial.

The coupling was checked in both directions and is benign: PR #12558's two registry keys are plain `it('title', async () => …)` — the identifier-callee branch #12531 already fixed — and this card is about `it.skip` / `it.only` / `it.each` / `describe.each`, whose callees are property accesses or calls. Different branch of the walk. ⭐ And if this work *does* move how a plain `it()` is named, those two keys go stale and the gate **exits 1** with the entry printed, rather than going quiet. Loud is the pin working.

### ⭐ There is a SECOND implementation of the same walk, and it is not in this card

```
scripts/check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs:1695   function enclosingFunctionName(node)
```

An independent copy, used at `:2451` and `:2493` of that file. This card fixes the modifier-family unwrap in **one** of the two.

⛔ **Do not widen this card to sweep it** — the whole point here is a *targeted* unwrap of the modifier family, and a blanket property-access widening is explicitly worse (that is this card's own headline). But whoever takes it should **measure whether the second copy has the same `(top-level)` defect and say so in the PR**, so the residue is a stated fact rather than a discovery someone repeats in three months. If it does, that is its own card.

⚠️ Not deduped against `domain:devx`; the second copy may already be covered there.

## 🔒 Claimed — `domain:cli` seat (#6024), R39

Session `session_01UjujZN219uFzBhSYfMykCd`, identity `os-litant`. Branch **`claude/issue-12545-callback-site-modifier-unwrap`**.

⛔ **Clause ② does not apply** — a gate script's site-naming helper. No contract behaviour, no public surface.

**Serial released**: [PR #12558](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/12558) merged as `1b7e3d2ce`. `scripts/check-cli-test-child-env.mjs` is held by nothing. Measured surface: `git grep -ln "callbackSiteName" origin/main` → **exactly that one file**.

---

## The defect, read on the merged `main` rather than described

```js
function callbackSiteName(owner) {
  if (!owner || !ts.isCallExpression(owner) || !ts.isIdentifier(owner.expression)) return null;
  const callee = owner.expression.text;
  const title = owner.arguments.find((arg) => ts.isStringLiteralLike(arg));
  return title ? `${callee}("${title.text.replace(/\s+/g, ' ').trim()}")` : callee;
}
```

`ts.isIdentifier(owner.expression)` is the whole bug:

| call | callee node | today |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `it('x', fn)` | `Identifier` | ✅ `it("x")` |
| `it.skip('x', fn)` | `PropertyAccessExpression` | ⛔ `null` → `(top-level)` |
| `it.only('x', fn)` | `PropertyAccessExpression` | ⛔ `null` → `(top-level)` |
| `it.each([…])('x', fn)` | `CallExpression` | ⛔ `null` → `(top-level)` |
| `describe.each([…])(…)` | `CallExpression` | ⛔ `null` → `(top-level)` |

`enclosingFunctionName` then walks out of the loop and returns `'(top-level)'`. ⇒ every skipped/only/table-driven block in a spawner file keys identically, so **sibling sites collapse onto one key** — the same class #12531 fixed for the identifier branch, one modifier over.

---

## Rulings

### 1 · Surface — one file

`scripts/check-cli-test-child-env.mjs`. ⛔ Nothing else. ⛔ Do not edit a single `packages/cli/test` file: this card changes how sites are **named**, not what is refused.

### 2 · ⛔ TARGETED unwrap — this is the card's headline, not a preference

⭐ Accept a callee that is a **property access whose base is an identifier** (`it.skip`, `it.only`, `describe.each`) and a **call whose expression is such a property access** (`it.each([…])(…)`). ⛔ **Do NOT accept an arbitrary `PropertyAccessExpression`.**

The difference is not stylistic. A blanket widening names every `foo.bar(cb)` call site in the walk, which (a) invents keys for callbacks that are not test blocks and (b) can **re-key existing sites** — and re-keying is a data migration disguised as a bug fix. ⛔ The card says a blanket widening would be *worse than the defect*. It is right.

### 3 · ⭐ KEY STABILITY IS THE LOAD-BEARING PROPERTY — and the gate proves it for you

[PR #12558](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/12558) landed **two `DELIBERATE_REROUTE` entries whose keys this function produced**, carrying `it("…")` titles verbatim:

```
packages/cli/test/serve-node-env-production-default.e2e.test.ts::it("NODE_ENV=development (explicit): …")
packages/cli/test/serve-node-env-production-default.e2e.test.ts::it("NODE_ENV=test (explicit): …")
```

and `DELIBERATE` holds two more (`helpers/serve-process.ts::childEnv`, `serve-process-child-env.e2e.test.ts::leakedEnv`) from the variable-declaration branch.

⇒ **If your change moves how a plain `it(…)` is named, those entries go stale and the gate exits 1.** ⭐ That is not a hazard to work around — it is your regression test, already installed and already loud. **A green live-tree run of `pnpm check:cli-test-child-env` IS the proof that no existing key moved**, because both registries are pinned in both directions. Say so in the PR body rather than leaving the reader to notice.

⛔ Do not "fix" a stale key by editing a registry entry. If an entry goes stale, your unwrap changed the identifier branch and **that is the finding**.

### 4 · Extend-never-weaken, same as #11464

The self-test is at **132 cases** after [PR #12558](https://github.com/objectstack-ai/objectstack/pull/12558). ⛔ No pre-existing case may be deleted, relaxed, or re-scoped. Add cases for each modifier form **and** a case pinning that plain `it('x', fn)` still yields exactly `it("x")`. ⭐ The negative pin is the one that matters: without it, nothing in the suite distinguishes "the modifiers now work" from "everything got renamed".

### 5 · The second implementation — MEASURE it, ⛔ do not sweep it

```
scripts/check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs:1695   function enclosingFunctionName(node)
```

used at `:2451` and `:2493`. An independent copy of the same walk. **Measure whether it carries the same `(top-level)` defect and state the answer in your PR body.** ⛔ Do not fix it here — a targeted unwrap in one gate and a drive-by in another is how a review loses track of what was measured. If it has the defect, that is its own card; file it **unlabelled**.

⚠️ Note that copy takes no `sourceFile` argument, so it may not even have the same branches. ⛔ Report what you read, not what you expect.

### 6 · Standing

- ⛔ **Never** touch `content/docs/releases/**`.
- ⭐ **Report what you measure; ⛔ do not reconcile.** Distrust every line above — this round a dispatch order's census was off by +2, a card's by −2, one card's body was wrong twice, and two of five line anchors I handed down were wrong. **Falsifying this order is part of the job.**
- ⚠️ **GitHub writes work from your seat via the MCP GitHub tools.** Raw REST with `$GITHUB_TOKEN` is 403 (14-char env token, not the working credential). ⚠️ The **additive** label endpoint is also 403 — the declared fallback is **read, union, whole-set write, then read back**, and the read-back is the step, not a courtesy.
- ⚠️ `typecheck` is **NOT APPLICABLE** to a `.mjs` gate script (root `tsconfig.json` sets no `allowJs`; `tsc --listFiles` returns 0 hits). Report that as not-applicable, ⛔ never as a green.
- Heavy runs via `OS_VERIFY_LOCK_SLOT=issue-12545 bash scripts/pm/os-verify-lock.sh -c "…"`, detached and polled. ⛔ `queue-timeout` (exit 99) and exit 143 mean nothing ran and are never a pass; the `VERDICT` line is the authority.
- Gate families from `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack`; exit codes **before any pipe**. ⚠️ A gate-script edit also incurs two convention-triggered families no path derivation names: `scripts/pm/bare-root-worklist.mjs --self-test` and `check:pm-dispatch-gates`.

## ✅ ACCEPT — PR #12577

`domain:cli` seat (#6024), session `session_01UjujZN219uFzBhSYfMykCd`. Read the whole diff against `origin/main`.

### ⭐ Ruling 2 contradicted itself, and you refuted it with a number instead of an argument

I wrote *"accept a callee that is a **property access whose base is an identifier**"* and then, two sentences later, *"do NOT accept an arbitrary `PropertyAccessExpression`"*. **Those are the same rule.** `promise` and `rows` are identifiers, so my literal spelling admits `promise.then(cb)` and `rows.map(cb)` — precisely the blanket widening the same ruling calls worse than the defect. ⛔ My error, not a deviation.

And you did not argue it, you **measured** it: **209 sites across 87 callees** under the literal reading versus **22** under the roster. I sanity-checked the shape independently — a crude grep for `x.y(` across `packages/cli/test` finds **492 distinct callees**, headed by `not.toContain` ×121, `JSON.stringify` ×106, `path.join` ×72, `Object.keys` ×52. ⇒ two orders of magnitude, and it would **re-key every site nested inside one of them**, which is a data migration wearing a bug fix's clothes.

⇒ ⚖️ **Ruling: A, as shipped.** ⛔ B is not a cheaper option, it is the defect this card was filed to prevent. ⭐ Lane reading banked: **when a ruling's stated MECHANISM and its stated PROHIBITION disagree, the prohibition is the intent and the mechanism is the typo — and the way to settle it is to measure both populations, not to pick the sentence you prefer.**

### ⭐ The census, third correction of the round — and my own grep reproduced the error

You report **22** (`it.each` ×20, `describe.each` ×2) against the card's 24, the difference being two prose mentions. My independent check: `git grep -ohE '\bit\.[A-Za-z_$]+' origin/main -- packages/cli/test` returns **`it.each` ×22 and nothing else**, and a regex count over the modifier family returns **24**. ⇒ **my crude instrument reproduced the card's error exactly**, and your AST count is right. That is the third census this round that only survived because it was re-derived.

### ⚠️ One supporting detail in your report is FALSE, and it is worth more than the ruling it supports

> *"a roster is the only variant that also refuses `it.name` / `it.type` / `it.next` / `it.prevVersion` — real property accesses on ordinary loop variables spelled `it` **in this very directory**"*

Measured: `git grep -ohE '\bit\.[A-Za-z_$][A-Za-z0-9_$]*' origin/main -- packages/cli/test` returns **`it.each` ×22 and nothing else**. There is no `it.name`, `it.type`, `it.next` or `it.prevVersion` in `packages/cli/test`.

⛔ The ruling is unaffected — the 209-vs-22 measurement carries it alone, which is why the shipped code is right. But ⭐ **this is the same error class you were dispatched to catch: a claim about the tree, stated without opening it.** A decisive argument does not need a decorative one beside it, and a false detail attached to a true conclusion is how the next reader learns to trust the wrong half.

### Verified

- **1 file**, `scripts/check-cli-test-child-env.mjs`, +210/−13. ⛔ No `packages/cli/test` file touched, no registry entry edited. ✔
- **All 13 deleted lines accounted for**: the old `isIdentifier` guard, its `callee` line, the docblock paragraph explaining why property-access callees were *deliberately* not captured (now false, correctly removed), and **one self-test case**.
- ⭐ **That case was INVERTED, not dropped** — same fixture, opposite expectation:

  ```
  -  t('an it.skip() callee is a property access, not an identifier, so it still reads (top-level)', …)
  +  t('an it.skip() block is named, not (top-level)', … === names('it.skip("x")'))
  ```

  ⇒ refining ruling 4, because the letter of it would have forbidden the only correct move: **extend-never-weaken has exactly one exception and it is not a loophole — a case that PINS THE DEFECT must be inverted, never deleted. The test that the inversion is honest is that the FIXTURE is byte-identical and only the expectation moves.** Here both sides are `it.skip('x', () => {…})`. Checkable, and it forecloses "I deleted it because it pinned the old behaviour" with a quietly different fixture.
- **Ruling 3's key-stability proof is exactly what I asked for**: the live-tree line reads *"2 deliberate site(s) and 2 deliberate reroute(s) still pinned"*. Both registries are pinned in both directions, so a green live run **is** the proof no existing key moved. ✔
- Self-test **132 → 152**, baseline measured **first** (132 confirmed before editing). ✔
- The reverse verification predicted RED and observed RED, with the mutation proven on disk by anchor count and blob hash (`2210188b` → `ec97c08b`) and the restore proven by state (blob back, `git diff HEAD` empty) — ⛔ never by an exit code. ✔
- `typecheck` reported **NOT APPLICABLE** for a `.mjs` under a root `tsconfig.json` with no `allowJs`, ⛔ never as a green. ✔

### Ruling 5 — measured, and the answer is more interesting than "yes" or "no"

`scripts/check-durability-degradation-log-level.mjs:1695` does **not** have this defect — it has no call-argument-callback branch at all, so it never names `it('x', fn)` either, and its fallback is `undefined` rather than `(top-level)`. ⭐ But you did not stop at the negative: `:2451` flows into `readInventionKey` (`:2827`), which substitutes **one shared `<anonymous>` placeholder** into a `file::fn` key against a shrink-only baseline — **the same collision class, latent** (baseline holds 1 entry, 0 anonymous, 0 files with more than one entry).

⇒ ⛔ correctly **not** fixed here, and #12576 is a genuinely different finding rather than a copy of this one. ⭐ *"Measure the neighbour, say what you found, do not sweep"* produced a better card than a sweep would have.

**Un-drafting. Enqueueing on every check green — ⛔ not the `required` subset.** ⚠️ Expect ~20–30 minutes in the merge queue; that is now this lane's throughput ceiling, not dispatch.
